title: Video desk, Fri Nov 27 (Black Friday) set: The SPY Tape, Mag 7 Scoreboard, Trading Explained (bid-ask spread), AI This Week

general-counsel-agent.note: All ten checks on file after reviewing the four review sheets (SPY tape, Mag 7 scoreboard, bid-ask spread explainer, AI this week), report.json spoken text, titles, captions and sources. Defamation screen: companies appear only with their own data or with figures reported by named outlets; no person is named. The market videos state no reason for any move and make no prediction; the AI video reports forecasts as forecasts and says what 'AI-influenced' and 'AI-referred' measure.

advertising-consumer-protection-counsel.note: Every number traces to a saved raw response or a cited source (factcheck.py: 0 unmatched). SPY and Mag 7 numbers come from prep.py's facts over the saved Webull 5-minute and daily bars; the six spreads are recomputed from the saved Webull order books (12:38:58 p.m. ET) and checked bar by bar. Adobe's +127% is the observed season-to-date figure (Digital Commerce 360, Nov 25; Tech Research Online), not the earlier forecast, and the video says these are clicks, not purchases. Salesforce's $75.8B is labelled a forecast of AI-influenced sales, with the definition on screen. Tidal: outlets differ on how many tracks will be removed (27M-29M), so no count is given. No 'best', 'guaranteed' or earnings claims.

email-anti-spam-compliance-counsel.note: No commercial email. The delivery email goes to the owner only.

privacy-data-protection-counsel.note: No personal data and no person named or shown. Order-book data is market-wide quote data with no account information.

copyright-fair-use-counsel.note: Charts and cards are drawn from data by the kit's renderers; the voice is Kokoro-82M (Apache-2.0); music is synthesized per video by music.py; fonts are Inter, Space Grotesk and JetBrains Mono (SIL OFL). News facts and the FINRA and J.P. Morgan definitions are restated in our own words with credit; no article text, images or logos are copied.

trademark-brand-clearance-counsel.note: SPY, QQQ, the Mag 7 tickers, Adobe, Salesforce, Tidal, Webull, FINRA, J.P. Morgan and the news outlets are named only to refer to them (nominative use); no logos and nothing suggests endorsement or affiliation. 'Magnificent 7' is used as the common market nickname for the seven stocks. Hashtags are generic, except #NVDA (the ticker of the week's leader) on the Mag 7 caption, as in earlier weeks.

financial-content-compliance-counsel.note: 'Educational only. Not financial advice.' is on screen and in the captions of the SPY tape, Mag 7 and bid-ask spread videos. No buy/sell call, target or prediction; no reason given for any move. The Mag 7 outro asks 'Who wins next week?' as an engagement question, the same as earlier weeks, with no pick. The explainer defines the spread and shows one moment's quotes; it does not tell viewers how or when to trade. The AI video has no market or investing claim.

platform-terms-policy-counsel.note: The narrator is a synthetic (AI) voice over data graphics: on Instagram and Facebook turn on the 'AI info' label. Nothing realistic depicts a real person, so YouTube's altered-content disclosure isn't triggered, but disclosing the AI voice is the safer choice. No paid partnership with any company named, so no branded-content tag. Every title is 100 characters or fewer (YouTube's limit): the AI title was cut from 110 to 89 and the recap title from about 110 to 90.

kids-content-coppa-counsel.note: All four are adult market, finance and tech-news content: not made for kids, no child appears, no child data is collected.

contracts-commercial-terms-counsel.note: No proposal, quote, offer or contract; nothing is sold or promised in these videos.

fixes_made: AI this week: the first searches came back from single aggregators (model releases, a leadership story, an IPO price range) with no second outlet; the scout switched to Black Friday AI-shopping data and the Tidal policy, each confirmed by 2+ outlets dated within 14 days.
Adobe's 95% Black Friday AI-traffic figure is its Sep 28 forecast (older than 14 days); the video uses Adobe's observed +127% season to date through Nov 22 instead.
SPY tape: prep.py's default hook and outro read like a full session; added that Black Friday was a half-day with the last 5-minute bar at 12:55 ET.
Mag 7: added that the week had four sessions because markets were closed Thursday for Thanksgiving.
Fact-check flagged '58', '360' and '9.53' as untraced; each was traced (quote time 12:38:58, the outlet name Digital Commerce 360, the day's high minus low) and kept.

Video Last Touch: three on-screen lines left one word alone on a line ('now', 'Morgan)', 'sales'); reworded to 'Bid: the most a buyer will pay', 'A cost of trading (J.P. Morgan)' / 'A sign of liquidity (J.P. Morgan)', and 'AI and agents to influence $75.8B of global online Cyber Week sales' (the source's own order), then both scene videos were re-rendered and re-checked.
Re-rendering the scene videos listed them twice in report.json and on the page; make_scenes.py now replaces an earlier entry for the same file (kit fix).
The 16:9 recap's title ran about 110 characters and dropped 'SPY'; page.py now names SPY and falls back to a shorter title to stay within YouTube's 100-character limit (kit fix).
The AI this week title was 110 characters; shortened to 89.
posting_notes: Instagram and Facebook: turn on the 'AI info' label (synthetic narrator voice).
YouTube: no realistic person is depicted, so the altered-content toggle isn't required, but turning it on for the AI voice is the safer choice.
The SPY tape and Mag 7 videos are about Fri Nov 27 and this week: post them by Monday Nov 30, or say the date in the post text.
The bid-ask spread video shows one moment's quotes (12:38 p.m. ET, Nov 27); spreads change all day, as the video says.
AI this week: the Adobe and Salesforce figures are their own data and forecasts as reported by the named outlets; Salesforce's is a forecast of AI-influenced sales, not agent purchases.
